b1-14-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Staying in Touch
b1-14-01.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks how you stay in touch with your sisters. You normally send messages during the day.
b1-14-01.prompt: Tell Carlos how you normally stay in touch with Lauren and Kaylee.
b1-14-01.target: Normalmente envío mensajes durante el día a mis hermanas.
b1-14-01.english: I normally send messages to my sisters during the day.
b1-14-01.canDo: I can describe current communication habits.

b1-14-02.title: Communicative Challenge: My New Phone
b1-14-02.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks what you have done with your phone. You have updated it recently, and now you use it differently.
b1-14-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you have done with your phone.
b1-14-02.english: I have updated my device recently.
b1-14-02.canDo: I can describe changes brought by technology.

b1-14-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Call or Message
b1-14-03.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks whether a video call is better than a message. A video call is more immediate than an email, although an email lets you think.
b1-14-03.prompt: Compare a video call with an email for Carlos.
b1-14-03.target: La videollamada es más inmediata que el correo electrónico, aunque el correo me permite pensar.
b1-14-03.english: A video call is more immediate than email, although email lets me think.

b1-14-04.title: Communicative Challenge: No Internet
b1-14-04.scenario: You are Carlos. In Budapest, Meg asks what you would do without internet. You would depend more on the phone.
b1-14-04.prompt: Tell Meg what would happen if you did not have internet.
b1-14-04.target: Si no tuviéramos internet, dependeríamos más del teléfono.
b1-14-04.english: If we did not have internet, we would depend more on the telephone.
b1-14-04.canDo: I can discuss life without technology.

b1-14-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Monastery Letter
b1-14-05.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks about the letter from a monastery that you read in Spanish. The writer walks in the cloister in the morning and talks with the villagers in the afternoon.
b1-14-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the writer does in the morning and in the afternoon.
cues: Say what he does in the morning
Say what he does in the afternoon
b1-14-05.target: Por la mañana el escritor sale a caminar por el claustro, y por la tarde conversa con los campesinos del pueblo.
b1-14-05.english: In the morning the writer goes for a walk in the cloister, and in the afternoon he talks with the villagers.
b1-14-05.canDo: I can discuss the effects of digital life.

b1-14-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Pros and Cons
b1-14-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. In Budapest, Carlos asks what you think of screens. You see an advantage and a disadvantage.
b1-14-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos one advantage and one disadvantage of technology.
cues: Say a disadvantage with a contrast
b1-14-consolidation.target: Por una parte, la tecnología facilita la comunicación; por otra parte, puede afectar a la privacidad.
b1-14-consolidation.english: On the one hand, technology makes communication easier; on the other hand, it can affect privacy.
b1-14-consolidation.canDo: I can consolidate technology and communication vocabulary.
